title: Talk it through 2.2
role: Colleague giving advice to someone who is afraid of a presentation
can_do: I can give advice and instructions to help someone overcome a fear.
I can calm someone down with firm, kind language and first conditional sentences.

nodes.partner_line: I am so afraid of speaking in front of the board tomorrow.
nodes.translation: Tengo mucho miedo de hablar frente a la junta mañana.

options.text: Take a deep breath. You are better prepared than you think.
Calm down. Nobody expects a perfect speech.
I understand. Let us go through your notes together.

nodes.partner_line: But what if I forget everything?
nodes.model_reply: If you forget a point, pause and check your notes.

nodes.partner_line: My hands shake when I stand up.
nodes.translation: Me tiemblan las manos cuando me pongo de pie.

options.text: If your hands shake, hold a pen or rest them on the table.
Do not worry about it. People rarely notice.
Breathe slowly and press your feet to the floor.

nodes.partner_line: Should I memorise the whole speech?

options.text: No, learn the key points and trust your preparation.
Rehearse it aloud twice, but do not memorise every word.
I would not. If you memorise it, you may sound stiff.

nodes.partner_line: Where should I look while I speak?

options.text: Focus on one friendly face at a time.
Look at different parts of the room, not at the floor.
Try to make eye contact with someone who nods.

nodes.partner_line: Thank you. I feel a bit calmer now.
nodes.translation: Gracias. Me siento un poco más tranquilo.

options.text: Good. If you need help tomorrow, I will be in the front row.
You will be fine. Get a good night's sleep.
I am glad. Remember to drink some water before you start.
